slides.texte_overlay:
Rare skills that will make you
unforgettable

Learn to introduce people properly. Not just "This is Mark." Say "This is Mark, he once drove across Canada in a car with no heater." Now two strangers have something to talk about, and they'll remember who did it.
Learn to host, even badly. Invite four people over, cook one big pot of pasta, put on a good playlist. People forget a hundred nights at the bar. They remember the night at your place.

Get good at toasts. Birthdays, weddings, a friend's new job. Thirty seconds, one specific memory, raise your glass. Most people mumble "Cheers, guys." Be the one who says something that actually lands.

Become the guy who knows random things. Five minutes a day of history, art or science. Like why the Eiffel Tower was only supposed to stay up for twenty years. People never forget the friend with the stories.
slides.texte_sophia: Become the guy who knows random things. A micro-learning app like the Sophia app gives you five minutes a day of history, art or science. People never forget the friend who always has a story.

slides.texte_overlay: Learn a proper handshake. Firm, two seconds, eye contact, then say their name back. "Good to meet you, Sarah." It sounds old school, and that's exactly why it stands out in a room full of awkward waves.

Send the follow-up. Met someone interesting? Send the article, the song, the place you talked about. "Saw this and thought of you." Five seconds of effort, and you go from stranger to someone they remember.

Never show up empty-handed. A bottle of wine, a dessert, a book you just finished and think they'd like. It doesn't have to cost much. It tells people you thought about them before you even walked in.
